demo.banner: Demo: nothing you type leaves your browser, and no message goes anywhere. Use your own photos.
demo.legal: This deployment is a demonstration with no server and no database behind it. What follows describes the service as it is built, not as this page runs it: here nothing you type is collected or stored, and none of it leaves your browser. The demo keeps one flag, strays-mock-session, in session storage while you are signed in to it. The map, once you turn it on, still loads from OpenStreetMap as described below.
demo.noWorker: This demo answers its own API calls from a service worker, and this browser did not let it start one. A regular, non-private window should work.

hero.lead: Someone recognises the cat on your street faster than any shelter database will. This is a board for that, and for the shelters rehoming the animals nobody came back for. Moderated before anything goes public.

sections.howLead: Three steps, and a moderator between every listing and the public page.
sections.stepOneBody: A photo and a spot on the map. No name and no number: whoever recognises the animal writes to you through the site.
sections.stepTwoBody: Every listing waits in a queue. Nothing reaches the public map before somebody has looked at the photo.
sections.stepThreeBody: The listing shows on the map for the neighbourhood it belongs to, and a message reaches you by email.

legal.contact: Questions, or a request about your own data:
legal.privacyIntro: What strays stores about you, why, for how long and who else sees it, both in the service behind the board and in your own browser. If this page and the copy kept with the code ever disagree, this page is what you relied on, and it wins.
legal.privacyWhoBody:
Nikolai Melnichenko, a private individual running strays as a free, non-commercial project, is the controller of the personal data described here.

Contact for anything about your data, a moderation decision or a report: nikolai.melnichenko.fe@gmail.com. Every email the service sends can be answered and reaches a person. There is no data protection officer; the law does not require one for a project this size.
legal.privacyWhatTitle: What is stored, why, and on what basis
legal.privacyWhatBody:
Email address: signing in, confirmation and reset links, email about your account and about moderation decisions. Basis: contract (GDPR art. 6(1)(b)).

Password: only an argon2 hash, for signing in. The password itself is never stored. Basis: contract.

Which version of the terms you accepted, and when: proof that you agreed to them and confirmed you are at least 16. Basis: contract and legal obligation.

Two-factor secret, encrypted, and hashes of the recovery codes: only if you turn two-factor sign in on. Basis: contract.

Sessions (when each started and when it was last used): so you can see and end the places you are signed in. Basis: contract, and legitimate interest in keeping your account safe.

Date of your last sign in: to delete accounts nobody uses any more. Basis: legitimate interest in not keeping data longer than needed.

Your listings (text, photos, city, point on the map): publishing them is the service. Basis: contract.

Messages you send about a listing: passed on to the listing's owner by email, then forgotten. Basis: contract.

Reports you file, and notices sent through the public form: getting illegal or misleading listings taken down. Basis: legal obligation under article 16 of the Digital Services Act, and legitimate interest in a safe board.

Moderation record and block reason: explaining decisions and handling appeals. Basis: legal obligation under article 17 of the Digital Services Act, and defending legal claims.

Request logs: keeping the service running and spotting abuse. Basis: legitimate interest in security.

Nothing is used for advertising, profiling or analytics, and nothing is sold. No decision about you is made by an automated system: every listing, report and block is decided by a person. No AI model reads your data or writes anything on the site.

You do not have to give any of this, but without an email address and a password there is no account, and without confirming the address you cannot post or write to anybody.
legal.privacyKeepBody:
An account whose email address was never confirmed: deleted 7 days after sign up.

An account nobody has signed in to: deleted after 2 years, with an email telling you it happened.

Any account: deleted at once when you delete it.

A listing: 180 days after it was posted, or 30 days after it was rejected.

A photo never attached to a listing: after 24 hours.

A session: 30 days after sign in, 7 days after its last use, or when you log out or end it.

Name and email address on a notice: as soon as the answer is sent.

A closed report: 180 days after it was closed.

Moderation record: after 1 year.

Request logs: after at most 30 days, by the hosting provider.

Database backups roll over within 7 days, so anything deleted is gone from them too by then.

Reset links work for an hour and confirmation links for a day, and each works once.
legal.privacyBrowserBody:
Three cookies, all strictly necessary for signing in: __Host-access proves you are signed in and lasts 15 minutes; __Host-refresh renews it and lasts until the session ends, 30 days at most; __Host-mfa holds a sign in between the password and the second factor for 5 minutes. All three are HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict.

Up to two keys in local storage, each written only when you ask for it: i18nextLng, if you pick a language with the switcher, and strays-map-tiles, if you choose to show the map.

The map is not loaded until you ask for it. When you do, your browser fetches the map tiles from the servers of the OpenStreetMap Foundation, in the United Kingdom, which see your IP address and the area you look at. That is the only request this site makes to anybody else. The fonts are served from this site, and there are no tracking pixels and no third-party scripts.

That is the whole list, and it is why there is no consent banner: everything on it is strictly necessary or set at your own request. Being exempt from asking is not being exempt from telling, which is what this section is for.
legal.privacyRightsBody:
You can ask to see what is held about you, to have it corrected or deleted, to restrict how it is used, to object to anything done on the basis of legitimate interests, and to receive your data in a portable format. Most of this you can do yourself, on your account page:

Download a copy: everything about your account as JSON, including your listings, the reports you filed, your sessions, the terms you accepted and moderation decisions about you.

Where you are signed in: see your sessions and end any of them.

Delete the account: removes it, its listings, photos and sessions at once. Two traces stay for their own retention period: the moderation record, which names an account id and not a person, and reports you filed, which lose the link to you.

For anything else, write to nikolai.melnichenko.fe@gmail.com. You get an answer within a month.

You can also complain to a data protection authority: in Portugal that is the Comissão Nacional de Proteção de Dados (www.cnpd.pt), or the authority where you live or work.
legal.termsIntro: These are the rules for using strays. Signing up means you accept them.
legal.termsPostBody:
A listing has to be about a real animal that is lost, found, or looking for a home, and has to be true as far as you know. In particular:

No selling. A listing may not offer an animal for money or advertise breeding. Shelters may mention their usual adoption fee.

Nothing illegal, including animals that may not be kept or traded, and content that infringes somebody else's rights.

Your own photos, or photos you are allowed to use.

No personal data in the listing. No phone numbers, addresses or names, yours or anybody else's. People reach you by writing through the site; we pass their message on by email, and your address stays private until you reply. Shelter animals link to the shelter's own site.

No spam, scams, insults, hate or harassment.

Every new or edited listing is read by a moderator before it goes public. A listing that breaks these rules is rejected or taken down.

You keep the rights to what you post. You allow strays to show it on the board for as long as the listing is up, and nowhere else.
legal.privacyDetailsBody:
Photos are re-encoded before they are stored, first on your device and again on the server, so nothing your phone wrote into the file survives, GPS position included. They sit in a private bucket and are only ever shown through links that expire within an hour.

Location: the public sees a listing's point rounded to about a hundred metres. The exact point is visible only to its owner and to moderators.

Writing to somebody about a listing: nobody's address is shown on the site. When you write about a listing, your message is emailed to its owner with your address as the one to reply to, so the owner learns your address and nobody else does. The owner's address stays private unless they answer you. The text of the message is not stored anywhere on our side; the log only notes that one account wrote to another about which listing.

Shelter listings are not reached through us: they link to the animal's page on the shelter's own site.

Request logs hold the method, path, status and timing of each request. They do not hold your IP address, your browser's headers or query strings. When a request is refused for being too fast or not allowed, the log names the account, or for a signed-out visitor only the network, with the last part of the address cut off. Rate limit counters do use the full address, in memory, and forget it within an hour.

Passwords against breaches: when you choose a password, the first five characters of its SHA-1 hash go to the Pwned Passwords service, which answers with every leaked hash starting the same way. Five characters match thousands of passwords, so nothing that identifies you or the password leaves the server.

Shelter feeds: some listings come from shelters that agreed in writing to share a feed of their animals. A shelter can withdraw at any time, and everything imported from it is removed at once.
legal.privacyProcessorsBody:
Each of these works on our instructions under a data processing agreement and gets only what it needs.

Railway hosts the application, the database and the cache, so it holds everything at rest. EU region.

Cloudflare R2 holds the photos, in an EU jurisdiction bucket. Cloudflare also serves this site.

Resend receives your email address and the text of each email we send you, including messages passed between users. United States.

All three are companies based in the United States. Where data leaves the European Economic Area, or a US provider could be asked for it, the transfer rests on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework for providers certified under it, and otherwise on the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses in that provider's data processing agreement.

Data is disclosed to anybody else only when the law requires it, for example a valid order from a court or the police.
legal.privacyChildrenBody: strays is for people aged 16 and over, and signing up includes confirming that. If you believe a younger person has an account, write to nikolai.melnichenko.fe@gmail.com and it will be deleted.
legal.privacyChangesBody: When this notice changes in a way that matters, the date at the top changes, and if it affects what is done with data you already gave, you get an email before it takes effect.
legal.termsWhoBody:
strays is run by Nikolai Melnichenko, a private individual, as a free and non-commercial project. There is no company behind it and nobody earns money from it.

Contact: nikolai.melnichenko.fe@gmail.com, in English or Portuguese. This is also the single point of contact for users and for authorities under articles 11 and 12 of the Digital Services Act.
legal.termsWhatBody:
A free board where people post animals they have found or lost and shelters post animals for adoption, so that the animal and its people find each other. strays only publishes what users and shelters write. It does not take part in any handover or adoption, and it does not check that what a listing says is true.

There are no fees, no paid features and no advertising.
legal.termsAccountBody:
You must be at least 16 to sign up, and you confirm that when you do. One account per person. Keep your password to yourself; you are responsible for what is posted from your account.

An account whose email address is not confirmed within 7 days is deleted, and so is an account nobody has signed in to for 2 years. You can delete your account yourself at any time.
legal.termsReportBody:
If a listing breaks these rules, use the report button on it when you are signed in.

If you believe a listing is illegal, anybody can tell us through the notice form linked under every listing and at the bottom of every page, without an account. Say which listing it is, why you think it is illegal, and give your name and email address. We confirm that we received it, a person decides, and we tell you the outcome. Your name and address are deleted once you have the answer, and are not shown to the person who posted the listing.

Somebody who keeps sending notices that are plainly unfounded may have further notices set aside for a while, after a warning.

If a listing or a notice suggests that somebody's life or safety is in danger, or that a crime of that kind is being committed, we pass what we have to the police, as article 18 of the Digital Services Act requires.
legal.termsSuspendBody: An account that posts something seriously illegal, or keeps breaking section 4 after listings were rejected, may be blocked. A blocked account cannot sign in and its listings are hidden. An account can also be blocked for abusing the report or notice forms.
legal.termsDecisionsBody:
Whenever a listing of yours is rejected or taken down, or your account is blocked, you get an email saying what was decided, the facts behind it, which section of these terms it rests on, whether it followed a report, and that a person made the decision.

If you disagree, reply to that email and somebody else will look at it again. You can also turn to an out-of-court dispute settlement body certified under article 21 of the Digital Services Act, or to a court. None of this takes away any other right you have.
legal.termsMeetingBody: Arranging to hand over or collect an animal means meeting somebody you do not know. Meet in a public place, and never pay anyone to get an animal back. strays cannot check the people who post and is not part of anything agreed between users.
legal.termsLiabilityBody: strays is offered as it is, free of charge, and may be unavailable at times or stop. Within what the law allows, strays is not liable for what users or shelters post, or for what happens between people who met through it. Nothing in these terms limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for anything else the law does not allow to be limited, and nothing takes away your rights as a consumer.
legal.termsChangesBody: When these terms change in a way that matters, you get an email at least 30 days before the new version applies. If you do not accept it, you can delete your account before then.
legal.termsLawBody: Portuguese law applies. If you are a consumer living elsewhere in the EU, you keep the protection of the law where you live and can bring a claim in your own courts. How your data is handled is set out on the privacy page.

notices.title: Report illegal content
notices.intro: For a listing you believe is illegal, whether or not you have an account. A person reads every notice, and you get the outcome by email. Your name and address are deleted once you have the answer and are never shown to whoever posted the listing. For a listing that is only wrong or spam, the report button on the listing is quicker.
